permission.title: Let TaxPlot find deductions for you
permission.sub: Most of your deductible payments already happen automatically — insurance auto-debit, PPF SIP, EMI. We can spot them so you don't have to remember to log anything.
permission.row1Desc: We scan only for bank/UPI debit notifications — never personal messages. Matched against known insurers, PPF, EMI lenders.
permission.row2Desc: One tap to confirm it's deductible — no photo needed for auto-detected payments.
permission.note: You can turn this off anytime in Settings. Nothing is sent to us until you confirm a detected payment — we never auto-save without your review. (This demo simulates detection locally — no SMS is actually read.)

quickconfirm.emptySub: No detected payments waiting right now.
quickconfirm.emptyNote: We'll notify you here as soon as we spot a new insurance, PPF, or EMI payment.
quickconfirm.sub: Detected from payment alerts — one tap to count them.
quickconfirm.addManually: 📷 Something else? Add a receipt manually

camera.overlayText: Fit the whole receipt in frame
camera.outlineHint: Tap the shutter, then choose a photo — real camera capture uses your device's camera roll in this demo.
camera.fallbackSub: Want to retake, or enter the details yourself?

dpdp.title: Before you add a photo
dpdp.what: The receipt photo and the details you confirm — vendor, amount, date, category.
dpdp.why: To work out which tax deduction it falls under, and show it on your dashboard and in your report.
dpdp.where: Only on this device, in this browser's own storage — nothing is uploaded to a server. Clearing your browser data, or your browser running low on space, can erase it, so use Settings → Your data to save a backup.
dpdp.delete: Settings → Your data → Delete my data erases all receipts, photos and answers from this device. Backup files you saved yourself are not affected. Reloading no longer clears them.

review.heading: Confirm this receipt
review.sub: We've filled this in — just check it's right.
review.subBlank: Fill in what you can — we'll remember it for your report.
review.rentPanRequiredNote: Your landlord's PAN is generally needed once annual rent is above {{amount}} (estimate of the current rule; your employer may ask earlier).
review.rentTdsWarning: Rent above {{threshold}}/month means you may need to deduct TDS under Section {{sectionNew}} (was {{sectionOld}}) — {{rate}}% with the landlord's PAN on file, {{noPanRate}}% without it.
review.rentPanAadhaarReminder: If your landlord's PAN isn't linked to their Aadhaar, a higher TDS rate can apply — worth checking before the year-end deduction.
review.familyNoneAdded: Add a {{relation}} in Settings → Family to tag whose this is.
review.microDisc: Saved amounts feed your dashboard estimate. Keep the original receipt/proof for filing — this app doesn't store legal proof of payment.
review.toastVendor: Add who this was paid to.
review.warnDuplicate: Saved — but this looks like a receipt you already logged (same payee, amount and date). Check your receipts list.
review.warnDateOutsideFY: Saved — but this date falls outside the current tax year. Double-check it's correct.
review.warnCash126Disallowed: Saved — but Section 126 (80D) premiums paid in cash generally aren't deductible. Only the preventive check-up line allows cash.
review.warnCash133OverLimit: Saved — but Section 133 (80G) cash donations above ₹2,000 aren't deductible. A non-cash payment would count in full.

nudge.declarationBody: Many employers ask for your Form 124 (was 12BB) declaration, often around April, including which regime you want. If you do nothing, they usually assume the new regime.
nudge.proofsBody: Many employers collect investment and rent proofs, roughly between December and February (some earlier or later). On the old regime, your Report tab has an employer proof pack grouped by section.
nudge.note: Timing varies by employer: check your payroll calendar. Estimate only, not tax advice.

todo.title: Do I need to do anything?
todo.body: On the new regime, usually not. The standard deduction ({{std}}) needs no proof, and if you give your employer no declaration they generally assume the new regime. You only need to submit investment proofs if you choose the old regime.
todo.note: Check your employer's payroll rules, which can differ. Estimate only, not tax advice.

storage.backupHelp: Save a copy of your receipts, photos and answers as a file you keep. The file is not encrypted, so store it somewhere private.
storage.restoreHelp: Restore from a backup file made here. This replaces what is on this device.
storage.badFile: That file is not a TaxPlot backup.
storage.saveFailed: Could not save on this device — storage may be full. Export a backup now.
storage.nearlyFull: Device storage for TaxPlot is nearly full. Export a backup and remove old photos.
storage.notPersisted: Your browser may clear TaxPlot data when space is low or the app is unused for a while. Keep a backup; adding the app to your home screen may help.

hraCheck.inputLabel: HRA exemption you plan to claim (per year)
hraCheck.inputPh: e.g. from your rent receipts or payslip
hraCheck.warn: The HRA exemption you entered ({{claimed}}) is about {{excess}} more than the {{estimate}} we estimated for you. Estimates can differ from your payslip, so please double-check your basic salary, HRA received, rent and city before claiming it.
hraCheck.ok: Your figure is within our HRA estimate. It is still only an estimate.
hraCheck.note: Claiming more than the rules allow can lead to a notice. Estimate only, not tax advice: confirm with your employer or a CA.

form130.title: Form 130 cross-check
form130.intro: Type figures from your Form 130 (salary tax certificate, was Form 16) and we compare them with what you have logged here. Nothing is fetched or sent anywhere.
form130.differsHelp: A difference is not necessarily an error: our figures are estimates, caps apply, and some items are not logged here. Check the original documents or ask a CA.
form130.tdsHelp: TDS is compared with our estimated tax. This is an estimate, not your final tax. A gap usually means a refund or some tax still to pay.
form130.empty: Enter at least one figure to compare.

freelance.title: Money received
freelance.estimate: If you are a professional covered by the scheme — presumptive scheme (Section 44ADA, new number to be verified): about {{pct}}% of receipts, {{profit}}, may be treated as profit. Estimate only, not your final tax.
freelance.digitalOnly: Above the lower limit the scheme needs almost all receipts to come digitally. Check with a CA.
freelance.overLimit: Receipts look above the presumptive scheme limit, so it may not apply. Check with a CA.
freelance.reminder: Advance tax reminder: freelancers on the presumptive scheme can pay the year's advance tax in one go by {{date}}; others pay in instalments. Confirm with a CA.

overview.savedSub: vs. claiming no deductions this year
overview.detectBannerMetaGeneric: Review to count them toward your deductions
overview.regimeCardTitleNewBetter: The New Regime is still lower for you
overview.regimeCardTitleOldBetter: The Old Regime is lower for you
overview.regimeCardBody: On what you've logged so far, it comes out {{amount}} cheaper. We re-check every time you add a receipt.
overview.oldRegimeNudgeTitle: The old tax regime works out cheaper
overview.oldRegimeNudgeBody: You'd pay {{amount}} less on the old tax regime. Tell your employer in April and your CA at filing time.
overview.emptyNote: No receipts logged yet. Snap your first one, or check Settings to turn on auto-detect.
overview.investmentsGloss: PPF, ELSS, life insurance, EPF, home loan principal, tuition fees
overview.extraNpsGloss: On top of Section 123 — separate {{cap}} bucket
overview.capNoteDone: Cap reached. Anything more here won't lower your tax.
overview.capNoteNone: If you pay this, it has its own cap on top of others.
overview.hraNote: Based on rent, salary and city. Log a rent receipt every month with the landlord's PAN — and check it's linked to their Aadhaar, since TDS can be higher if it isn't.
overview.donationsNote: 50% or 100% deductible depending on the fund — we'll flag which when you add the receipt.
overview.newRegimeMeta: Standard Deduction {{std}} · rebate if taxable income is up to {{threshold}}
overview.newRegimeBody: Most Section 123 (80C) and 126 (80D) style deductions don't apply here. We keep logging your receipts so you can compare at filing time. Your estimate: {{status}}.
overview.compareTie: Old and New Regime work out the same for you this year, based on what you've logged.
overview.compareOldCheaper: Old Regime would actually be {{amount}} cheaper for you this year, based on what you've logged.
overview.compareNewCheaper: New Regime is {{amount}} cheaper than Old Regime for you this year, based on what you've logged.

receipts.emptyAllNote: No receipts yet — snap your first one, or enter one manually.
receipts.emptyFilterNote: No receipts in this filter yet.

report.emptyReport: No deductions logged yet this year — snap a receipt to start building your report.
report.missedDeadlineBody: Missing the proof cut-off at work usually means more tax is deducted from your salary for now, not a lost deduction. Under the old regime, genuine deductions can generally still be claimed when you file your return, and tax deducted in excess may come back as a refund. Keep your proofs.
report.missedDeadlineNote: Informational only. Based on how this worked under earlier rules; we have not confirmed the 2025 Act wording. Ask your payroll team what they can still accept, and confirm with a CA.
report.missedHeader: A few things you didn't log this year
report.employerPackNote: A simpler PDF grouped by section, for your employer's Jan–Feb Form 124 (was 12BB) investment declaration — not a tax computation.
report.postFilingRevisedDeadline: Revised return due by {{date}}, if you need to correct anything.
report.missedHealthSelf: No health insurance premium logged for yourself or family — if you paid one, add it before we finalize this report.
report.missedHealthParents: No health insurance premium logged for parents — if you pay one, it has its own Section 126 (80D) cap on top of your own.
report.missedHomeLoan: Home loan: no interest logged yet. Ask your lender for the year's interest certificate — it is the proof for Section 22 (24(b)) interest.
report.missedHomeLoanCert: Home loan: ask your lender for the year's interest certificate — it is the proof for Section 22 (24(b)) interest.
report.missedRentNoHra: You pay rent but get no HRA — Section 134 (80GG) may apply to you under the old regime. Keep rent receipts and your landlord's details; conditions apply (for example, no HRA received, no home owned in your city), so check with a CA.
report.missedDonations: No donations logged — Section 133 (80G) gifts may still qualify.
report.missedNps: No extra NPS (Section 124) logged — an easy {{amount}} top-up bucket if you have room.
report.missedPreventiveCheckup: No preventive health checkup logged — it counts inside your Section 126 (80D) self/family cap, up to {{amount}}, even if paid in cash.
report.missedTuition: No tuition fees logged — the tuition component (not admission, transport or hostel fees) counts under Section 123 (80C), old regime only, for up to two children.
report.bigDisclaimer: This is an informational estimate based on what you logged — not a filed tax computation. Confirm final figures with your CA or the official portal before filing.
report.footerDisclaimer: Informational estimate — not tax advice. Not a filed return; cannot be submitted to the Income Tax Department. Keep the original receipt/proof for filing — this PDF doesn't store legal proof of payment.

returns.note: A starting pointer taken only from the client type (salaried or not): not a filing decision and not tax advice: the CA confirms the right form and the current due date for each client.

room.title: Room left under each section
room.sub: Pick a section to see which clients can still claim more. Amounts are estimates from logged receipts.
room.none: Nobody has room left under this section.
room.bulkNote: The bulk message has no names or amounts, so you can paste it into a WhatsApp broadcast list. Each button opens WhatsApp with the message ready. You choose the contact and press send; TaxPlot does not send anything.
room.messageOne: Hi {{name}}, a factual note on your {{fy}} records: you have {{amount}} room left under {{sec}} (limit {{cap}}, estimate from receipts logged so far; it counts only under the old regime). Not tax advice, and no action needed if this is already covered.
room.messageAll: Hi, a factual note on your {{fy}} records: you may have room left under {{sec}} (limit {{cap}}, old regime only). Reply and I will share my estimate for you.
room.noneOldRegime: No client is better off on the old regime at current figures, so there is no deduction room to nudge about. This list fills in for clients whose old-regime estimate is lower.

election.label: Regime on record
election.detail: On record: {{elected}} regime. The estimate from logged receipts puts the {{better}} regime lower by about {{amount}}. Worth confirming with the client which regime they intend; this is a prompt to check, not a recommendation, and the final figures can differ. TaxPlot does not change any election.
election.ok: On record: {{elected}} regime, same as the lower estimate.
election.note: Regime on record is sample data here. The flag compares it with the estimate only; it is informational, not tax advice.

landlord.detail: Landlord PAN not on record. It is generally needed when annual rent is above {{threshold}} (estimate of the current rule). Rent on record: {{rent}} a year. Ask the client; TaxPlot does not check or submit it.
landlord.ok: Landlord PAN on file for the rent recorded ({{rent}} a year).
landlord.note: Rent and landlord PAN on record are sample data here. The threshold is an estimate of the current rule.
